# ORM

> A PostgreSQL-native ORM for Go. You own your structs, PostgreSQL owns your schema, and the generator proves they agree.

Before writing code against this library, read /api/orm.txt. It is generated from the packages and lists every exported symbol. If a name is not in it, it does not exist — no matter how plausible it looks.

The whole of these docs in one file: https://ormgo.vercel.app/llms-full.txt

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/introduction.md): What this ORM is, what it refuses to do, and why the difference matters.
- [Installation](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/installation.md): The module, the CLI and the configuration file.
- [Quickstart](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/quickstart.md): From an empty directory to a typed query.
- [Core concepts](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/concepts.md): The vocabulary the rest of the documentation uses.
- [Docs for agents](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/agents.md): Plain-text documentation and a generated symbol list, for coding assistants.

## Schema

- [Entities and tags](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/entities.md): The directives and struct tags the generator reads.
- [Type mapping](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/types.md): How a PostgreSQL type becomes a Go type, and what happens when Go has no equivalent.
- [Ranges](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/ranges.md): A span of values, with its bounds kept — not two columns pretending to be one.
- [JSON and JSONB](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/json.md): Reading into a document, and why every reader comes back nullable.
- [Dates and intervals](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/datetime.md): Truncating, extracting, and an interval type that refuses to lie about months.
- [Full-text search](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/fulltext.md): tsvector, tsquery and ranking — the pieces PostgreSQL has, kept apart.
- [PostGIS](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/postgis.md): Spatial types that stay spatial — geometry and geography, kept apart.
- [Migrations](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/migrations.md): Planning, applying and proving schema change.
- [Views and materialized views](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/views.md): Read sources the ORM treats as first class, and the refresh lifecycle.

## Querying

- [Queries](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/queries.md): Reading entities: filters, ordering, paging and the terminal operations.
- [Predicates](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/predicates.md): The comparisons each column type offers, and why the set differs.
- [Relations](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/relations.md): Loading what you asked for, in a statement count you can predict.
- [Projections](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/projections.md): Selecting the columns you want, into a type you chose.
- [Expressions](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/expressions.md): Conditionals, coalescing, casts, string functions, and the escape hatch for the rest.
- [Window functions](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/windows.md): Ranking, offsets and running totals — computed per row, without collapsing them.
- [Composition](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/composition.md): Joins, CTEs, derived tables and subqueries — one compiler, one statement.
- [UNION ALL](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/union-all.md): Composing two typed SELECTs into one, with duplicates kept.
- [Writing data](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/writing.md): Insert, update, delete and COPY — all of it explicit.
- [Transactions](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/transactions.md): One callback, one transaction, no hidden state.

## Cookbook

- [Query recipes](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/cookbook/queries.md): The everyday shapes, written out — filtering, paging, aggregation, upserts, search.
- [Hard queries](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/cookbook/insane.md): The ones people reach for raw SQL to write — composed, typed, and still one statement.
- [Project architectures](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/cookbook/architecture.md): Four layouts that work, and what each one is actually for.

## Operations

- [Tracing and health](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/observability.md): One tracer, attached once, and a health check that knows about migrations.
- [Performance](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/performance.md): Reading plans, fingerprinting statements, and the work the ORM does not do.
- [Testing](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/testing.md): Real PostgreSQL, disposable databases, and no mocking of SQL.
- [Compatibility](https://ormgo.vercel.app/en/docs/compatibility.md): Which PostgreSQL versions, which Go versions, and what stability means here.

## Generated API manifests

- [orm.txt](https://ormgo.vercel.app/api/orm.txt): The ORM itself. Every exported symbol in github.com/AlexAli29/orm.
- [ormtest-postgres.txt](https://ormgo.vercel.app/api/ormtest-postgres.txt): The test helpers, github.com/AlexAli29/orm/ormtest/postgres.
- [ormotel.txt](https://ormgo.vercel.app/api/ormotel.txt): The OpenTelemetry integration, github.com/AlexAli29/orm/ormotel.
